query: what is the difference between the latin grammys and the grammys
title: What is the difference between the Latin Grammys and the Grammys?
answer: The Latin Grammys are a separate awards show run by the Latin Recording Academy for music performed mainly in Spanish or Portuguese, from Latin America, Spain, Portugal and Latino communities in the U.S. and Canada. The Grammys are run by the Recording Academy. The 27th Latin Grammys air Nov. 12, 2026, from Las Vegas.
body:
The Recording Academy, which presents the Grammys, formed the Latin Recording Academy in 1997, and the first Latin Grammy ceremony was held on Sept. 13, 2000, at the Staples Center in Los Angeles. Organizers said the "Latin music universe was deemed too large to fit on the Grammy Awards." Winners are chosen by a peer vote of the Latin academy's members, who live in the U.S., Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula.

To qualify, a recording must be at least 60% in Spanish or Portuguese (the threshold was 51% before 2024) and be released in North, Central or South America, the Caribbean, Spain or Portugal. Recordings in other Ibero-American languages, such as Catalan, Basque, Galician, Quechua and Guarani, can be accepted by a majority vote. The eligibility year runs from June 1 to May 30. Like the Grammys, the show has four genre-free general categories: Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year and Best New Artist.

The 2026 ceremony, sometimes stylized "Latin GRAMMYs," takes place at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on Thursday, Nov. 12. The broadcast starts at 8 p.m. ET on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX, with Roselyn Sánchez hosting for the 10th time. Edgar Barrera leads with 10 nominations, and Karol G, Rosalía, Jorge Drexler and Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso have seven each.
in_the_news: The 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards take place Nov. 12, 2026, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas.

faq.q: Are the Latin Grammys the same as the Grammys?
faq.a: No. They are run by a different organization, the Latin Recording Academy, and held as a separate ceremony with their own eligibility rules and voters.

faq.q: Who votes for the Latin Grammys?
faq.a: Voting members of the Latin Recording Academy, who are music professionals living in the U.S., Latin America, Spain and Portugal.

faq.q: What language do songs need to be in for the Latin Grammys?
faq.a: At least 60% of the content must be in Spanish or Portuguese. Some other Ibero-American languages, such as Catalan or Quechua, can be accepted by majority vote.
Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, at 8 p.m. ET, with a one-hour preshow at 7 p.m. ET, from the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas.

faq.q: What channel are the Latin Grammys on?
faq.a: Univision, UniMás and Galavisión, and streaming on ViX.

faq.q: When did the Latin Grammys start?
faq.a: The first ceremony was held on Sept. 13, 2000, in Los Angeles.
